text: I kicked Hawthorne out because he failed to see how organised we are. He became a liability, so I removed him. Do not make me explain your departure the same way.
Thomas needed parades, statues, crowds chanting his name. I prefer officials who understand an instruction the first time.
You thought we opposed Hawthorne because he was ruthless? We opposed him because he was reckless. There is a considerable difference.
He announced every ambition before he had the means to achieve it. By the time he declared himself indispensable, I had already replaced his people.
The Federation survived because someone was willing to decide who could be sacrificed. You were spared those meetings.
I never intended for you to live past Antarctica, you know. When they reported that you had awakened, I assumed the cold would finish what we started.
YOU WERE SUPPOSED TO WAKE UP ALONE, CONFUSED, WITH NOTHING BUT ICE BETWEEN YOU AND THE NEAREST LIVING SOUL!
THEN BROWN FOUND YOU. ONE UNSCHEDULED ACT OF KINDNESS, AND SUDDENLY I HAD A SURVIVOR WHERE THERE SHOULD HAVE BEEN A BODY!
DO YOU KNOW HOW MANY REPORTS I BURIED? HOW MANY PEOPLE I HAD TO REASSURE THAT YOU WOULD NEVER MAKE IT OFF THAT CONTINENT?
I SHOULD HAVE SENT SOMEONE TO THAT RESEARCH STATION THE MOMENT YOU OPENED YOUR EYES! I WILL NOT LEAVE YOUR DEATH TO THE WEATHER AGAIN!
I have been in charge of this dwarf planet for over a billion years. You are hardly the first invader to mistake it for an easy conquest.
I welcomed you into my court, Wanderer. Was that merely an opportunity to study its defences?
Hawthorne wanted my throne. Alexia betrayed my trust. Tell me—what excuse have you brought?
These people survived exile and occupation. I will not ask them to endure you as well.
You feel that cold creeping through your armour? Keep fighting. It will reach your hands soon.
I remember when your ancestors had yet to discover fire. Age has taught me patience, but you are exhausting it.
Look behind you. Those soldiers once cheered your arrival. Now they are defending their homes against you.
Do not mistake my restraint for weakness. There are parts of this palace I am willing to bury beneath the ice.
We could have faced the darkness together. Instead, you have given it one less battle to fight.
Come, then. If you insist on taking Eris, you will have to get past its empress.
